appraisal_events.evidence: Malgré mes supplications, elle sortit de la chambre... le protocole de Françoise ne le permettait pas, elle aurait manqué de délicatesse envers ce brave homme, l'état de ma grand'mère ne comptait plus. Souci caractéristique de Combray, de ne pas manquer à la délicatesse.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically exposes Françoise's rigid Combray code of social 'délicatesse,' which leads her to leave the dying grandmother's side to attend to an electrician's feelings; her genuine love for the grandmother is acknowledged but her priorities are shown as misplaced.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle ne vit plus du tout... elle fut sourde... l'embarras de la parole augmenta. On était obligé de faire répéter à ma grand'mère à peu près tout ce qu'elle disait... elle renonçait à prononcer un seul mot... n'articulait que des sons inintelligibles... on l'empêchait, autant qu'on pouvait, de [se lever], de peur qu'elle ne se rendît compte de sa paralysie.
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage narrates the grandmother's progressive loss of sight, hearing, speech, and physical autonomy, staging her as increasingly excluded from communication and self-determination, and treated as an object to be managed and shielded from the truth of her own state.

status_effects.explanation: Françoise's judgment is locally lowered as the narrator exposes the misplaced priorities of her code of delicacy at a moment of urgency, even though her affection for the grandmother is not denied.
The grandmother loses the capacity to see, hear, and speak intelligibly, stripping her of the means to communicate or assert herself.
She is increasingly managed and kept from full awareness of her own paralysis, excluded from agency over her own situation.

ambiguities: Françoise's portrayal is layered: the narrator both affirms her genuine devotion to the grandmother and ironizes the rigid social code that leads her to prioritize the electrician's feelings, so the evaluation is not purely negative.
